reviews.title: Investing Everywhere but the User Experience
reviews.text:
Letterboxd is an excellent concept undermined by persistent reliability problems. The service suffers from recurring outages and server instability, but the bigger issue is that even when the site is technically “up,” core functionality can be unreliable. Changes to Watchlists, Lists, reviews, ratings, and other account data can take an unreasonably long time to propagate or fail to appear where they should at all. A change being successfully saved should not mean waiting 10+ minutes before the rest of the site recognizes it.

This is especially frustrating for paying users because these aren't merely cosmetic bugs; they undermine the basic premise of a database-driven service. Filters and other features can produce stale or incorrect results because they aren't consistently reflecting the user's own data. Letterboxd has built an indispensable product and community, but its infrastructure and data reliability increasingly feel like an afterthought. For a paid service, recurring downtime and inconsistent data synchronization are difficult to justify, and users deserve substantially better transparency and reliability.

I have such little confidence in their servers that I now have a schedule to routinely backup my account data. This is the only platform I use that requires such handholding and nuance.

The service also lacks the privacy features one would expect from any mature platform of this kind. Privacy is a right, not a privilege. The absence of fundamental user privacy

reviews.title: Just ban the pop-up ads man
reviews.text:
I love this app and I use it every day. You get ads on the free version and they’re kind of annoying of course, but nothing intolerable, it doesn’t ruin the app for me. This past month however they’ve allowed these new stupid pop-up ads that make the app unusable. The ads force at least one, up to 10 layered, full-screen video pop-ups (just AI art and some generic ad-copy slop), and the malware follows you across the entire app once it’s been activated, so you can’t even just close them all and be done with it. Has caused me to just give up and close the app many a time.

There’s no in-app way to report ads for being spam/inappropriate/etc, so I have no recourse it seems besides leaving a review on here. You can’t force me into buying premium by making your app unusable, I will just stop using it. Ban that advertiser, and no more pop-ups please.

Also the new Letterboxd store on the main page is annoyingly emphasized by the UI. Quit that

reviews.title: Intrusive ads, frequent crashing
reviews.text:
I really love the interface of the app, it makes logging films and exploring the reviews other people leave really simple and intuitive. What ruins the experience are the egregiously intrusive ads that constantly interrupt you while you use the app. I’m not stupid, I can accept that if you don’t pay for premium, you’re going to have ads. That’s fine. What is not fine is the extent to which those ads force their way past the actual content of the app. The videos that cover almost a quarter of the screen while you’re trying to browse are bad enough, but it’s the recent development of pop-up ads that cover THE ENTIRE SCREEN periodically, with no discernible reason or warning during the time I’m using the app, including WHILE I’M TRYING TO TYPE A REVIEW that really make me reconsider using this app at all. 

It also doesn’t help that the app has a lot of struggles not crashing at times. For example, I just logged and rated a movie and the app crashed: 1) after I logged the movie as “watched,” 2) after I “liked” the movie, and then finally 3) after I published my review. 

It boggles my mind that, despite all the money they must be getting from absolutely assaulting you with ads, they can’t make an app that reliably works. It doesn’t make me so annoyed that I want to pay to get rid of the ads, it just makes me more adamant that I should never ever give letterboxd any of my money.
